text.p: VIENNA, July 24 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Thursday are:
DIE PRESSE
- Ruling coalition partners SPOe and OeVP agree to cooperate more closely, notably on the NATO dispute and to vote the same way on key issues in parliament.
- Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend, a conservative, said his party the OeVP would not leave the coalition due to the question of Austrian membership of NATO.

- The double budget for 1998 and 1999 goes before parliament on Thursday but unions and the workers' chamber have yet to nod their approval after negotiations over pension measures went late into the night without agreement.
- The Vienna ATX index ended at a new record high thanks to buoyant international markets.
- The economics chamber expects Austria's trade deficit to slip slightly this year.
- Salomon Brothers raises its recommendation on Bank Austria's preference shares to "strong buy" from "buy".
- Agriculture Minister Wilhelm Molterer criticises EU reforms, saying there is too little compensation.
- Hirsch Servo, the first company to list on the Vienna bourse's "fit" segment, said it had reached its ambitious targets for earnings in the business year 1996/97.
- Economic research institute Wifo says the liberalisation of the telecoms industry from 1998 would not cause a "job miracle" and would therefore not solve Austria's unemployment problems.
DER STANDARD
- Economic researchers largely agree with Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger's forecast of 2.9 percent GDP growth in 1999.
WIRTSCHAFTS BLATT
- The Vienna stock market clocked up its biggest gains in five years thanks to buying from British and American investors.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- The government was not able to work out details of pension reform before today's budget. Pension reform will now wait until autumn.
- Salzburg is hoping to hold the Winter Olympics in 2006 and will present its ideas to the Austrian Olympic Committee in September.
- At least five Austrians were killed in a bus crash on the Greek island of Rhodes. One further Austrian was seriously injured, four lightly injured.
- The liberalisation of telecomunications will create at best only 3000 jobs, according to a Wifo research report.
- The appreciation of sterling makes holidays in Austria cheaper for Britons.
- Austria's trade deficit could narrow by six billion schillings, according to the economics chamber. Last year the trade balance had a hole measuring 100 billion schillings.
